'''Lucinda''' "'''Lucie'''" '''Green''' (born 1975<ref name="asteroid"/>) is a British [[science communication|science communicator]] and [[solar physics|solar physicist]].

Green is a Professor of Physics and a Royal Society University Research Fellow (previously the Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellow) at [[Mullard Space Science Laboratory]] (MSSL) of the [[University College London|University College London (UCL)]].<ref name="msslwelcome">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mssl.ucl.ac.uk/~lmg/Welcome.html |title=Welcome |author=Lucie Green |publisher=[[Mullard Space Science Laboratory]] |access-date= 5 April 2015 }}</ref><ref name="bust" /> Green runs MSSL's public engagement programme and sits on the board of the [[European Solar Physics Division]] of the [[European Physical Society]] and the advisory board of the [[Science Museum, London|Science Museum]].<ref name="msslwelcome" />

In 2013, Green became the first ever female presenter of ''[[The Sky at Night]]'' following the death of [[Patrick Moore|Sir Patrick Moore]].<ref name="bednews2">{{Cite web |author=Sophie Scott |date=8 February 2013 |title=The sky's the limit for Dame Alice's Dr Lucie |url=http://www.bedfordshire-news.co.uk/skys-limit-Dame-Alices-Dr-Lucie/story-21721714-detail/story.html |access-date=5 April 2015 |publisher=Bedfordshire News}}{{dead link|date=March 2025}}</ref>

Green's research focuses primarily on the atmospheric activities of the [[Sun]], particularly [[coronal mass ejection]]s and the changes in the Sun's magnetic field which triggers them.<ref name="msslwelcome" /><ref name="msslresearch">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mssl.ucl.ac.uk/~lmg/My_research.html|title=My research |author=Lucie Green |publisher=[[Mullard Space Science Laboratory]] |access-date= 5 April 2015 }}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Green was born in {{Birth based on age as of date|35|2010|10|17|noage=y}}.<ref name=Bednews1>{{cite web|url=http://www.bedfordshire-news.co.uk/Lucies-love-astrophysics-makes-best/story-21716270-detail/story.html|title=Lucie's love for astrophysics makes her one of the best|author=Hazel Slade|publisher=Bedfordshire News|date=17 October 2010|access-date=5 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923183308/http://www.bedfordshire-news.co.uk/Lucies-love-astrophysics-makes-best/story-21716270-detail/story.html|archive-date=23 September 2015}}</ref> She attended [[Dame Alice Harpur School]] in Bedfordshire,<ref name="suntrek">{{Cite web |url=http://www.suntrek.org/solar-guides/lucy-green.shtml |title=Lucie Green - solar guides|publisher=Sun Trek |access-date=5 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126133810/https://www.mssl.ucl.ac.uk/jobs/careers/lmg.shtml |archive-date=26 January 2022}}</ref> gaining 9 GCSEs and 4 A-levels.<ref name="bednews2" /><ref name="suntrek"/><ref name=msslcareers/> After school she initially studied art,<ref name="hiw"/> before deciding later to study [[physics]].<ref name="hiw"/> She graduated with a 2:1 [[Master of Physics]] degree in physics with [[astrophysics]] from the [[University of Sussex]].<ref name="suntrek"/> In 2002, Green completed her PhD in solar physics at the [[Mullard Space Science Laboratory|MSSL]], University College London.<ref name="msslcareers" />

She returns to her school to discuss her research. Fiona Clements, Green's former physics teacher at the school, has said, “She is a great advocate for young women in science and we are proud that she continues to remember the school by returning to talk about her research to pupils."<ref name="Bednews1" />

"I always liked physics from an early age while I was at school. That was my passion: problem-solving or asking questions and then finding out ways of answering those questions. But I never had a burning ambition of being a space scientist, and I wasn’t even into amateur astronomy [at that time]."<ref name="hiw">{{Cite web |url=http://www.howitworksdaily.com/interview-dr-lucie-green/ |title=Interview: Dr Lucie Green |author=Laura Mears |publisher=How It Works |date=16 May 2013 |access-date=5 April 2015 }}</ref>

==Career==
[[File:Solar Flare Moon Eclipse NASA SDO AIA CME FQTQ 1.gif|thumb|261x261px|Images captured by the [[Solar Dynamics Observatory]] showing a [[solar eclipse]] followed by a M6.6 [[solar flare]].]]
After gaining her PhD, she moved to [[Cardiff University]]'s School of Physics and Astronomy <ref name=msslcareers >{{Cite web |url=http://www.mssl.ucl.ac.uk/jobs/careers/lmg.shtml |title=Dr. Lucie Green |publisher=[[Mullard Space Science Laboratory]] |access-date=5 April 2015 }}</ref><ref name="eureka">{{Cite web |url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2003-11/cu-tp112803.php |title=£9million telescope project brings astronomy into school classroom |publisher=Eureka Alert |date=28 November 2003 |access-date= 5 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080512172213/http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2003-11/cu-tp112803.php |archive-date=12 May 2008}}</ref> and became the Project Co-ordinator of the [[Faulkes Telescope Project]]. The project enables schools to have remote use of two two-metre class telescopes located in Hawaii ([[Faulkes Telescope North]] in [[Hawaii]]) and Australia ([[Faulkes Telescope South]] in [[Australia]]).<ref name="suntrek"/><ref name="eureka"/><ref name= Faulkes>{{Cite web |url=http://www.faulkes-telescope.com/news/453 |title=Close approach of asteroid Toutatis |publisher=[[Faulkes Telescope Project]]|date=2008 |access-date=5 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150911223521/https://www.faulkes-telescope.com/news/453 |archive-date=11 September 2015}}</ref>

Green is a Professor of Physics and a [[Leverhulme Trust|Leverhulme]] Research Fellow (previously the Royal Society Dorothy Hodgkin Fellow), at [[Mullard Space Science Laboratory|MSSL]]. Her current work focuses on the pattern of magnetic fields in the Sun's atmosphere, which sporadically erupt to form a [[coronal mass ejection]]; how these relate to geomagnetic activity and what this means for those living on the Earth.<ref name="msslwelcome" />

From 2006 to 2012, she was a member of the Royal Society's Education Committee and was part of their State of the Nation reports Working Group during 2007–2009.<ref name="msslwelcome" /> She is member of UCL's Steering Committee for the Beacon for Public Engagement. She also runs MSSL's public engagement programme.<ref name="msslwelcome" /><ref name="nesbit">{{Cite web |url=http://www.janklowandnesbit.co.uk/lucie-green |title=Lucie Green |publisher=Janklow & Nesbit UK |access-date=5 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105063342/https://www.janklowandnesbit.co.uk/lucie-green |archive-date=5 November 2013}}</ref>

===Solar Orbiter===
Green is involved in the development of the [[Solar Orbiter]], a [[Sun]]-observing [[satellite]] under development by the [[European Space Agency|ESA]].<ref name="nesbit" /> The aim of the mission is to perform close-up, high-resolution studies of the Sun for a better understanding of its behaviour, [[heliosphere]], solar wind and coronal magnetic field.<ref name="orbiter">{{Cite web|url=http://www.esa.int/Our_Activities/Space_Science/Solar_Orbiter|title=Solar Orbiter|publisher= European Space Agency|date=13 April 2015|access-date=18 April 2015 }}</ref>

==Media appearances==
Green regularly appears on television and radio, most notably ''[[The Sky at Night]]'', ''[[Stargazing Live]]'', ''Stardate'', ''[[Horizon (BBC TV series)|Horizon]]'', ''[[Xchange (TV series)|Xchange]]'' and ''[[The One Show]]''.<ref name="suerider">{{Cite web|url=http://www.sueridermanagement.co.uk/presenters/LucieGreen/LucieGreen.htm|title=Lucie Green|publisher=Sue Rider Management|date=2011|access-date=15 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304083137/http://www.sueridermanagement.co.uk/presenters/LucieGreen/LucieGreen.htm|archive-date=4 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her radio programmes include ''[[The Infinite Monkey Cage]]'', ''Saturday Live'' and ''PM'' ([[BBC Radio 4]]), ''Material World'', ''Slooh Radio'' (US), ''[[Newshour]]'' ([[BBC World Service]]), ''Live Drive'' and ''Bacon's Theory'' (BBC 5 Live), and ''The Butcher's Apron'' and ''Nick Ferrari'' (LBC).<ref name=suerider/>

Between 2004 and 2005 Green co-presented several programmes in the BBC/Open University series ''Stardate''. Episodes include "Stardate: Mission To Titan"<ref name="titan">{{Cite web |url=http://www.open.edu/openlearn/whats-on/tv/stardate-mission-titan |title=Stardate: Mission To Titan |author=The Stardate team |publisher=OpenLearn |date=11 January 2005 |access-date= 5 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313004131/https://www.open.edu/openlearn/whats-on/tv/stardate-mission-titan |archive-date=13 March 2014}}</ref> which she co-presented with [[Adam Hart-Davis]],<ref name="msslmedia">{{Cite web |url=http://www.mssl.ucl.ac.uk/~lmg/Media.html |title=Media work|author=Lucie Green  |publisher=[[Mullard Space Science Laboratory]] |access-date= 5 April 2015 }}</ref> covering the European Space Agency successfully landing the [[Huygens (spacecraft)|Huygens]] probe on [[Saturn]]'s largest moon, [[Titan (moon)|Titan]],<ref name="msslmedia"/> and "Stardate: Deep Impact"<ref name="deepimpact">{{Cite web |url=http://www.open.edu/openlearn/whats-on/tv/about-the-deep-impact-programme |title=OU on the BBC: Stardate: Deep Impact |author=The Stardate team  |publisher=OpenLearn |date=5 July 2007 |access-date=5 April 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313004056/https://www.open.edu/openlearn/whats-on/tv/about-the-deep-impact-programme |archive-date=13 March 2014}}</ref> which she co-presented with [[Brian Cox (physicist)|Brian Cox]], covering NASA successfully colliding a probe into the side of comet [[Tempel 1]] in an effort to learn more about the origins of the [[Solar System]].<ref name="msslmedia"/><ref name="deepimpact"/>

Since 2010, Green has appeared on and co-presented several episodes of ''Stargazing Live''<ref name=suerider/> and has appeared on several episodes of the BBC Radio 4 show ''The Infinite Monkey Cage'', discussing topics such as [[Global catastrophic risk|the end of the world]] and [[Multiverse|parallel universes]].<ref name="msslmedia"/><ref>{{cite web|url = https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b00snr0w/episodes/player|title = BBC Radio 4 - The Infinite Monkey Cage - Episodes|publisher = BBC|access-date = 23 June 2014}}</ref>

In 2013, Green hosted her own radio programme, ''Solar Max'' on BBC Radio 4 on the topic of [[space weather]]. The programme explained how emissions from the sun can cause changes in the Earth's magnetic field and upper atmosphere, and what the implications of these are for the UK.<ref name="msslmedia"/>

==Personal life==
When asked where her love of space science came from, Green has said: "As a child, I remember hearing my parents say that they thought I was going to be an astrophysicist when I grew up. Not actually knowing what an astro-thinga-me-wotsit was, I agreed with them because I thought it sounded impressive. Really at that time I wanted to look after animals. People used to bring me injured birds and I would stay up all night feeding them worms!"<ref name="suntrek"/>

In 2014, Green married stand-up comedian and maths communicator [[Matt Parker]].<ref name="Usborne">{{cite web|author=Simon Usborne |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/books/features/standup-mathematician-matt-parker-is-using-comedy-nights-to-preach-maths-to-big-audiences-9829504.html |title="Stand-up mathematician" Matt Parker is using comedy nights to preach maths to big audiences |work=The Independent |date=2014-10-30 |access-date=2015-12-12}}</ref> The couple used wedding rings made of [[meteoric iron]].<ref name="Usborne" />

==Awards and honours==
[[File:LucieGreenAtQEDcon2015-3.jpg|alt=Lucie Green presenting at QEDcon 2015|thumb|330x330px|Lucie Green presenting at QEDcon 2015]]
In 2005, Green was a member of a team that won a [[Royal Television Society]]'s Life Long Learning and Multimedia Award for a television show covering the [[transit of Venus]], that enabled viewers to make their own Sun-Earth distance measurements using observations of the transit that year.<ref name=suerider/><ref name="msslmedia"/><ref name="venustransit">{{Cite web |url=http://www.open.edu/openlearn/science-maths-technology/science/physics-and-astronomy/astronomy/measure-the-astronomical-unit-and-watch-the-transit-venus|title=Measure the Astronomical Unit and watch the Transit Of Venus |author= The Stardate team|publisher=OpenLearn|date= 25 March 2008|access-date=19 April 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140313035045/https://www.open.edu/openlearn/science-maths-technology/science/physics-and-astronomy/astronomy/measure-the-astronomical-unit-and-watch-the-transit-venus|archive-date=13 March 2014}}</ref>

Green has won awards for her contribution to public engagement with science. In 2009, she was awarded the [[Royal Society]]'s [[Kohn Award]] for Excellence in Engaging the Public with Science, for her work engaging a diverse audience with science, and more specifically, for creating a culture of public engagement within her department.<ref name="nesbit" /><ref name="kohn">{{Cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2009/space-scientist/ |title=Space scientist wins Royal Society award for science communication |publisher=The Royal Society |date=24 August 2009 |access-date=5 April 2015}}</ref>

In 2010, she was named, in ''[[The Times]]'' October science supplement, Eureka, as one of the UK top ten best science educators under 40.<ref name="Bednews1" />

In 2015, Green had a bust unveiled at the Royal Society in London, whilst being honoured at an event exploring the history of women and science writing. The bust was created and gifted to the Royal Society by [[Marcus Cornish]].<ref name=bust>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ucl.ac.uk/mssl/solar/news/mssl-solar-news/Lucie-Royal-Society|title=Bust of Lucie Green unveiled at the Royal Society|publisher=[[University College London]]|date=11 March 2015|access-date=7 April 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160310074602/https://www.ucl.ac.uk/mssl/solar/news/mssl-solar-news/Lucie-Royal-Society|archive-date=10 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> That year, Green was also awarded an Engineering and Physical Sciences [[Suffrage Science award|Suffrage Science]] Award.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-03-12|title=Suffrage Science 2015: Is the world of science pale, male and stale?|url=https://lms.mrc.ac.uk/suffrage-science-2015-world-science-pale-male-stale/|access-date=2021-05-13|website=LMS London Institute of Medical Sciences|language=en}}</ref>

In 2017, Green won the [[Lise Meitner Medal and Prize]] of the [[Institute of Physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.iop.org/about/awards/silver-subject-medals/lise-meitner-medal-and-prize-recipients|title=Lise Meitner Medal and Prize recipients|publisher=Institute of Physics|access-date=17 September 2020}}</ref>

In 2025, the [[main belt asteroid]] {{mp|2005 LG|31}} was named {{LoMP|180932|180932 Luciegreen}} in her honour.<ref name="asteroid">{{Citation|url=https://www.wgsbn-iau.org/files/Bulletins/V005/WGSBNBull_V005_019.pdf#page=9|journal=WGSBN Bulletin|volume=5|number=19|page=9|date=11 August 2025|title=(180932) Luciegreen = 2005 LG31|publisher=[[International Astronomical Union]]}}</ref>
